meta: Process, orbital welding (ASME IX), validation, controls, field service and quality jobs on PW and WFI systems in Canada. Pay range in every posting.

headline: Build systems that pass inspection
lead: We design, weld, test, qualify and service Purified Water (PW), Water for Injection (WFI) and pure steam systems for plants that answer to Health Canada, FDA and EU inspectors. Every weld, test and change leaves a signed record, and the people who make those records are the people we hire. This page says what each job involves, what you need to bring, where it is based, how much it travels and what it pays, so you can decide before you apply.

blocks.h: What the work is, and who it suits
body: Our systems are small enough that one engineer can know the whole of one, and regulated enough that every detail is written down. A process engineer reads the user requirement specification (URS) and draws the piping and instrumentation diagram (P&ID). A welder joins the 316L tubing and logs each weld. A validation specialist tests the system against a protocol the client approved. A field technician keeps it running for years after. You see the system you worked on pass its factory acceptance test (FAT), often with the client's quality team in the room.

The work suits people who like exact work and do not mind showing it. Documentation is about half of every job here: a weld without its log entry, or a test without its signed record, does not count. Field roles travel, and plant shutdowns fall on weekends and holidays. We say that up front because it is the main reason people leave this kind of work.

You do not need pharmaceutical experience for every role. We train good documentation practice and the standards we design to. [Confirm how many of the current team came from other industries, for example food, dairy, power or general process work, before publishing this sentence]

blocks.h: The roles we hire for, and where the work is described
rows: Process engineer

Review the client's URS and feed water analysis, size PW, WFI and pure steam systems, draw P&IDs, write the functional and equipment specifications, and design to USP <1231>, ISPE Baseline Guide Vol. 4 and ASME BPE. You answer design questions at FAT and through change control after handover
[Open or closed · posting reference]
Orbital welder

Make autogenous orbital welds in 316L stainless steel tubing to ASME BPE, from the weld map on the isometric. Run the sample weld (coupon), inspect by borescope, and log each weld with its procedure, weld schedule and the EN 10204 3.1 heat numbers of the parts it joins
[Open or closed · posting reference]
Validation specialist (commissioning and qualification)

Write and execute FAT, site acceptance test (SAT), installation qualification (IQ) and operational qualification (OQ) protocols, support the client's performance qualification (PQ), raise and close deviations, and assemble the turnover package to EU GMP Annex 15
[Open or closed · posting reference]
Controls and automation engineer

Program the programmable logic controller (PLC) and human-machine interface (HMI), design alarms, interlocks and sanitization sequences, configure audit trails to 21 CFR Part 11 and EU GMP Annex 11, write the software specifications to GAMP 5, and test the software at FAT and OQ
[Open or closed · posting reference]
Field service technician

Commission systems on site, run preventive maintenance, calibrate conductivity, total organic carbon (TOC) and flow instruments, replace membranes and lamps, run sanitizations and find faults, all under the client's change control and with a signed service record
[Open or closed · posting reference]
Quality specialist

Run document control, nonconformance reports and corrective and preventive action (CAPA) under our ISO 9001 quality system, review material certificates and weld records, check each turnover package before it leaves, and host client supplier audits
[Open or closed · posting reference]

blocks.h: Where each role touches one system

items.d: The process engineer sizes the system from the URS; the controls engineer writes the functional specification. Quality opens the project file.
The welders build the skid and loop in our shop from the weld map. Quality reviews heat certificates and weld logs as the work goes, not at the end.
Validation runs the FAT wet in our test bay against the approved protocol, with the process and controls engineers there to answer the client.
Field service installs and commissions on site; validation executes SAT, IQ and OQ and hands over the turnover package.
Field service maintains and calibrates the system under the client's change control. A change that touches the design goes back to the engineer who designed it.

items.q: I am not ASME Section IX qualified on orbital welding yet. Can I apply?
items.a: Yes, if you weld tube or pipe with GTAW. The practical interview includes a test weld on our procedure. [Confirm whether Aquemi qualifies welders who pass, and whether trainee welder positions exist]
No. We assess what you have done, wherever you did it. Engineers who sign drawings must hold a licence in the province concerned; provincial regulators assess experience gained abroad.

items.q: How much do field roles really travel?
items.a: The share for each role is in the requirements table and in every posting, with how travel time, meals and accommodation are paid. Shutdown work is planned [notice for planned shutdown work, weeks] ahead where the client allows.

items.q: Why does every posting show a pay range?
items.a: British Columbia has required it in public postings since 1 November 2023, and Ontario since 1 January 2026 for employers with 25 or more employees. We state it in every province because it saves both sides a call. The range is what we expect to pay for the role.
